The provided text explicitly states: 'Instead of approximating the non-linear projection function, we draw inspiration from the classical literature of Unscented Kalman Filter [16] and approximate the 3D Gaussian particles using a set of carefully selected sigma points... after which a 2D Gaussian can be re-estimated from them in form of a Unscented Transform (UT) [12].' - **Precision:** The UT avoids the linearization errors inherent in EWA splatting, which increase with camera distortion [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that EWA splatting relies on linearization (first-order approximation via Jacobian) which leads to approximation errors that 'become progressively worse with increasing distortion' [S1]. It further states that the Unscented Transform (UT) approximates the particle using sigma points which are projected exactly, thereby avoiding the linearization errors inherent in the Jacobian-based approach of EWA splatting.
